title: Dedicated capacity lab report and automated remediation plan for noisy-neighbor events
creator: Sofia Liang
description:
Summary: A capacity event on 2026-02-27 exposed weaknesses in how we size tenant reservations and how the burst-credit governor handled a noisy tenant with pathological KV cache churn. This ticket consolidates experimental findings from the incident lab, captures root-cause hypotheses validated by tests, and proposes an automated remediation plan (detection -> containment -> adaptive sizing -> rollback) to reduce time-to-recovery for future events.

Problem framing: During a sustained spike, a single tenant consumed disproportionate GPU cycles and inflated KV cache churn. Our soft-reservation decay and burst-credit scheme allowed prolonged overuse which caused eviction storms and tail-latency regressions for co-tenants. Postmortem telemetry showed three correlated signals: (1) long-running prefix drop rate increases, (2) reservation utilization > 140% for the offender for > 5 minutes, (3) burst-credit queue starvation on other tenants.

Goals: 1) Shorten detection-to-containment window to <= 60s for high-impact events. 2) Limit single-tenant eviction impact to <1% increased P95 across tenants. 3) Fully automate a safe correction path that can: scale down offender burst credit, enforce temporary hard cap for extreme behavior, and re-rightsize reservation with minimal manual review.

Scope: Dedicated GPU pools only. This ticket coordinates experimentation in the lab cluster, telemetry dashboard updates, operator runbook changes, and implementation of a controller that runs in the control-plane to remediate in three phases: detect, contain, repair.
summary_of_experiments: Baseline capture: replayed sampled traffic from 02-27 into lab cluster with tenant mix of 120 tenants and 1 synthetic noisy workload producing high KV churn
Experiment A - short hysteresis: reduced soft-reservation decay window from 10m -> 90s. Result: eviction rate down 58% but offender experienced 8% higher token-rejection rate; co-tenant P95 improved.

Experiment B - burst-credit governor rewrite: changed credit refill algorithm to proportional fairness with per-tenant cap. Result: sustained throughput for small tenants recovered; under extreme loads offender throttled earlier, reducing overall GPU saturation by 35%.

Experiment C - KV cache fingerprinting + rapid fencing: add lightweight fingerprint to detect pathological cache churn and apply temporary 2m fence (zero burst) to matching tenant. Result: immediate drop in cross-tenant tail latency; false positive rate measured at 0.3% in synthetic run.

Experiment D - autosizer feedback loop: autosize reservation up to 1.5x when utilization > 120% for > 3m, with human-review label for > 2x changes. Result: easier recovery for normal scale-ups but opened a window for repeated oscillation; added dampening solved oscillation in follow-up runs.
root_cause_hypotheses: Mis-sized reservations for a minority of tenants (historically due to conservative estimation) allowed tenants to rely on burst credits longer than intended, causing prolonged overheating.
Burst-credit governor was first-come-first-serve in practice for small time windows, enabling noisy tenants to starve others during sustained spikes.
Lack of fast, signal-driven containment (we only had human-in-the-loop escalation) increased blast radius before mitigation could be applied.
KV cache churn increased memory pressure and led to repeated cache invalidation, which amplified compute usage per request.
Telemetry thresholds were too coarse — detection required minute-scale aggregates rather than second-scale anomalies.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Adopt a staged automated remediation controller: detect -> contain -> repair. Tradeoff: a conservative fence may temporarily reduce throughput for the offender but keeps platform SLAs for co-tenants.
Use proportional-fair refill for burst-credit rather than strict priority queues. Tradeoff: slightly lower max single-tenant throughput but far better fairness under contention.
Make autosizer changes opt-out by default for enterprise tenants in Dedicated contracts to avoid surprise billing. Tradeoff: some tenants will require manual right-sizing conversations.

Fingerprint-based KV churn detection will be lightweight and sampling-based to keep CPU overhead low. Tradeoff: slight FP/FN risk that we mitigate with a short probation period and human-review for borderline cases.

acceptance_criteria: Detection: Alert fires within 60s of an offender crossing utilization >120% and sustained for 90s
Containment: Automated fence reduces offender burst credit to 0 or enforces hard cap and reduces cluster-wide GPU saturation by >=25% within 3 minutes
Repair: Autosizer suggests new reservation and either applies it automatically for <1.5x changes or flags for human review for >=1.5x changes
Observability: New Grafana panels reflect per-tenant eviction, KV churn fingerprint rate, and credit burn-rate; historical comparison available for last 30 days
Safety: False-positive fence rate <1% in synthetic validation runs and safe rollback exercised in QA
